page: Microsoft Azure D160als_v7 is a high-core compute-optimized virtual machine from the Dalsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 160 vCPUs mapped to 80 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The server utilizes the x86_64 architecture and provides 320.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include any onboard GPUs or local storage, though it is premium storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance across multiple compute and memory metrics. The server achieves top 10% placement in stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, as well as PassMark CPU and extended instruction benchmarks. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only small block cached bandwidth reaching 14528.43 GB/sec and large block uncached read bandwidth at 463.81 GB/sec. Cryptographic and compression capabilities are also strong, evidenced by top-tier results in gzip compression and bzip3 decompression.

The primary tradeoff of the D160als_v7 is its low memory density of 2.0 GB per core and the complete absence of local storage, requiring external storage attachments. However, this configuration offers high qualitative cost efficiency for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. It is highly suited for multi-threaded CPU-bound tasks, static web serving, high-throughput Redis operations, and CPU-based LLM inference, where it demonstrates strong to top-tier token generation speeds.
